note: Service: the Political Constitution of the Republic of Panama (the text WIPO Lex holds), Article 310: Panama shall have no army; all Panamanians are bound to take up arms to defend national independence and the State's territory, a duty with no peacetime call-up, so none is held. Work: not held. The same Constitution forbids work by minors under 14 (and night work under 16) save the exceptions the law sets, and lets the working day of those of 14 to 18 be cut to six hours; the Labour Code (1971, Article 117 by secondary reports) and the Family Code, which would say whether a performer under 14 may work and on what permit, weren't reached: the Ministry of Labour's site (mitradel.gob.pa) answers behind Incapsula and the Judiciary's code library (organojudicial.gob.pa/cendoj) behind a captcha, neither passed; a search on 2026-10-31 found no official text. Majority: not read; the Civil Code and Family Code weren't reached for the same reasons.

sources.title: WIPO Lex, Constitución Política de la República de Panamá (official text held by WIPO Lex)
sources.said: ARTICULO 310. La República de Panamá no tendrá ejército. ... Se prohíbe el trabajo a los menores de catorce años y el nocturno a los menores de dieciséis, salvo las excepciones que establezca la Ley.
